extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks to evaluate the mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly curated datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering 7 mathematical reasoning types and 5 primary tasks across diverse visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. In International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR). arXiv:2310.02255
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA compiles instances from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly curated datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For existing VQA datasets, heuristic rules based on numeric answers or quantity words were used for initial automatic filtering, followed by manual labeling by three expert annotators with majority voting. For the new datasets, questions were created and annotated based on puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots from online education resources, and academic papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (including Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA, ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, and VQA-AS), online learning platforms, online education resources, and academic papers released on Huggingface in August 2023.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic filtering using a dictionary of quantity words and numeric answers to select math-related candidates from VQA datasets; capping each source dataset at up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation; partitioning into a 1,000-example testmini set and a 5,141-example test set using stratified random sampling based on threshold and proportions; and normalizing extracted answers into standard formats (option letter, integer, float, list).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Candidate VQA problems were labeled by three expert annotators using custom web interfaces to verify whether they required mathematical reasoning. The three newly curated datasets (736 questions) were independently authored and annotated by graduate students in STEM fields in a two-step process: independent annotation by three reviewers followed by discussion and consensus resolution for discrepancies. Coarse mathematical reasoning category labels were derived from source metadata and verified through manual annotation on a 1,000-example sample.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom graphic user interface (GUI) annotation tools
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for identifying mathematical problems from VQA datasets achieved a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775. The newly curated datasets had an inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% (disagreements in only 6 of 736 questions). For mathematical reasoning category labeling, 94.1% of sampled examples had an exact match between automatic and human labels, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields and qualified expert annotators
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is partitioned into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples). Answer labels for the test set will remain unreleased to prevent data contamination, supported by an online evaluation platform. The authors commit to maintaining the dataset (including refining potential data noise based on community feedback) and evolving the evaluation leaderboard as new models emerge.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to advance the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of solving mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, such as educational assistance, logical analysis of statistical data, and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Potential gaps in coverage for certain mathematical problems and visuals; labor-intensive curation process limiting scalability and generalizability to broader domains; heterogeneity of annotations inherited from source datasets lacking a unified format or structure, with only 85.6% having detailed solution annotations; evaluation focused strictly on recent foundation models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing, Validation, and Benchmarking of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) for mathematical and visual reasoning capabilities.
